topic: The Shannon conjecture following Eq. (69), Section V.C, arXiv:2411.05766v1
title: A counterexample to the Shannon conjecture following Eq. (69) in Tarabunga et al., Section V.C

creators.name: Zhang, Wenlin
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: The Shannon conjecture following Eq. (69) in Section V.C of Tarabunga et al., arXiv:2411.05766v1, is false. An explicit three-qubit state has stabilizer-basis entropy log 4, whereas the proposed absolute-amplitude lower bound is log 16 - (9/8) log 3 > log 4. The same construction refutes the bound for nonnegative amplitudes, and continuity gives strictly positive examples. It extends to every N >= 3 and to a range of Renyi indices containing one. The collision entropy of the comparison distribution remains a valid Shannon lower bound for arbitrary affine supports. For amplitudes of constant modulus on each affine coset, the original bound holds at every Renyi index; this includes the source's Figure 1 product states.
summary: An exact three-qubit counterexample, positive-amplitude extensions, and a valid collision-entropy lower bound.
posing_locator: arXiv v1: Section V.C, Eq. (69) on p. 9, explicit Shannon conjecture on p. 10; related Appendix C.1-C.2, pp. 15-16. Journal version: Section 5.3, conjecture following Eq. (74).

verification_scope.lean_statement: Negation of the full-support Shannon bound via the signed three-qubit witness
written_proofs: Real-amplitude reduction with explicit quadratic phase conversion
All-index fixed-R minimum for the witness
Collision-entropy bound for arbitrary affine supports
All-index validity on coset-flat amplitudes and Figure 1 inputs
finite_checks: All 64 phase choices for the nonnegative three-qubit state at R=I3
Rational entropy intervals for a strictly positive example
